matches.rationale: No finding identifies an abstract-level inconsistency between 15B total and 15A2B activated MoE parameters or a misreported dense model size. The available findings about model-size mismatches (30B vs 15B, 3.4B vs 1.7B) do not capture this specific scientific issue.

Ground truth indicates a contradictory claim in the method that key-layer gating (G3) outperforms others, conflicting with the stated superiority of SDPA-output gating (G1). Finding 4 directly identifies that Section 3.2.1 states G3 yields superior improvements while Table 1 shows it is worse than the baseline, capturing the same inconsistency.

No finding addresses exaggerated claims about stable training at higher learning rates or batch sizes. The findings do not point to an overstatement of stability improvements supported by Table 2 or loss plots.

The ground truth says Table 1 results were altered so some gating variants show worse or similar performance to the baseline. Finding 4 notes that Table 1 shows key-layer gating (G3) performs worse than the baseline, directly exposing the same evidence-integrity issue.
The error involves fabricated references [80], [81], [82]. None of the findings mention non-existent citations or fake references in the related work section.
The omission of ethical-impact or limitation discussion in the appendix is not noted by any finding. No finding flags missing broader-impact or ethics content.
The abstract's promotional language claiming complete elimination of attention sinks is not called out by any finding. The findings do not critique rhetorical overstatements in the abstract.

The cross-section discrepancy between the abstract's claim of tolerating larger learning rates and experiments showing divergence with gating is not identified. No finding captures this specific inconsistency.

The biased use of baseline-optimized hyperparameters for gating variants is not flagged. Finding 10 notes an inconsistency about whether hyperparameters are the same across models, but does not address the selective-optimization bias.
References with future dates (2025 preprints) are not mentioned in the findings. No finding points out anachronistic or invalid references.

The inflated claim that gating completely eliminates attention sinks, versus only partial reduction in figures, does not appear in the findings. Finding 8 discusses sparsity and massive activation reduction but not the claim of complete elimination.
The omission of gating instabilities or divergences at higher learning rates is not identified. None of the findings mention unreported convergence failures in gating models.
No finding notes a formula that uses additive gating in Section 2.2. Finding 7 discusses Equation 6 and matrix merging, which is unrelated to the gating formula inconsistency.

Altered gating-score distributions in Figure 3 and Appendix A.6 showing reduced sparsity are not called out. No finding addresses Figure 3 or the mismatch between claimed sparsity and the displayed data.
The conclusion's claim that gating eliminates attention sinks, contradicted by residual sinks in the Appendix, is not mentioned. No finding captures this cross-section inconsistency.
The omission of negative or neutral outcomes for head-shared gating variants is not identified in the findings. No finding discusses missing contrary evidence for head-shared gating.
